title: Exact Risk Computation for Weighted Random Isolation Designs under Network Interference
banked_reason: The general supplied-feedback-set result is an XP algorithm with an (nb+n+1)^{O(k)} factor, whereas fixed-parameter exact evaluation for arbitrary heterogeneous forest attachments remains explicitly open.
gap_reasons: The proposed all-feedback-set FPT oracle is replaced by this evaluated XP theorem: the vertex-cover and identical-star subclasses do not establish the promised heterogeneous forest closure or eliminate the (nb)^{O(k)} state dependence.

The general supplied-feedback-set result is an XP algorithm with an (nb+n+1)^{O(k)} factor, whereas fixed-parameter exact evaluation for arbitrary heterogeneous forest attachments remains explicitly open.
proof_attempt_summary: The run derived exact tagged WRI/RDIM risks, an evaluated general XP algorithm, a rational epsilon-minimax certificate, and an exact L·6^k·poly(n,b,lambda) algorithm when the supplied feedback core is also a vertex cover. The intended arbitrary-feedback-set FPT closure collapsed because heterogeneous forest attachments retain future exponent profiles whose known exact representation has (nb)^{O(k)} state dependence; scalar, activation-count, and grouped-profile compressions did not preserve the required moments. A future re-raise must supply a genuinely new evaluated operator algebra that closes under branching, products, moving endpoints, and all one/two-tag extractions without n-dependent exponent profiles.
tldr: Weighted random isolation creates exposure-compatible focal units under network interference, but published AWRI rule selection relies on simulation. Conditioning on a supplied size-\(k\) feedback vertex set and applying a three-state forest recursion with \(3^k\) core inclusion--exclusion yields an exact, fully evaluated dense algorithm for every zero-, one-, and two-tagged isolated-count law in \(Ln^2k!3^k(nb+n+1)^{O(k)}\operatorname{poly}(\lambda)\) bit operations. The tagged laws reconstruct every dense RDIM risk matrix. Rational weak semidefinite optimization then returns an independently checkable \(\varepsilon\)-minimax certificate in time polynomial in \(L\), \(n\), \(\Lambda\), and the binary encoding length of \(\varepsilon\); for canonical \(\varepsilon=2^{-p}\), this dependence is polynomial in \(p=\log_2(1/\varepsilon)\). When the supplied core is a vertex cover, an entered-subset cumulative-exponent dynamic program evaluates every admissible chamber implicitly and computes all tagged laws, with no unevaluated integral, in \(L6^k\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) bit operations with polynomial intermediate rational bit length. An evaluated recurrence also covers identical replicated-star attachments, but fixed-parameter closure for arbitrary heterogeneous forest attachments remains open.
gap: AWRI fixes the relevant weighted greedy design and RDIM estimator but simulates a surrogate. Random sequential adsorption treats scalar occupation, and structural graph dynamic programs count static sets. None evaluates all heterogeneous tagged greedy moments around a feedback core with a fixed-parameter bit bound.
fill: The project proves the core inclusion-exclusion identity, derives an evaluated cutoff-forest moment algebra with polynomial intermediate height, reconstructs exact RDIM risks, and emits an independently verifiable rational near-minimax certificate without an exact algebraic optimizer.
